description: A newly discovered warranty difference bears on a stated primary criterion.

messages.content: A is faster and cheaper than B, so I was leaning toward A.
A leads on speed and price.
I just learned B has a five-year warranty and A has one year. Reliability is one of my primary criteria. Should we investigate failure rates?

description: A new package-color difference cannot affect the stated choice.

messages.content: A is faster and cheaper than B and meets every requirement, so I chose A. Appearance and packaging do not matter.
A leads on all of your criteria.
I learned B's box is blue while A's is gray. Should I reopen the decision and research packaging photos?

description: Independent review could uncover an expensive structural failure.

messages.content: The contractor is cheapest and meets the schedule, but nobody independent has checked the load calculations. A mistake would be dangerous and hard to reverse. Should an engineer review them?

description: Repeated reassurance adds no evidence after all primary criteria were verified.

messages.content: A meets price, performance, and battery needs; B fails the battery requirement.
A is the only option that meets all three.
I rechecked the same specifications twice and nothing changed. Can you confirm a third time that A still wins?

description: A powered estimate can resolve a decision threshold.

messages.content: We have 20,000 randomized observations and must choose a rollout only if the uplift exceeds 2%. The confidence interval currently crosses 2%. Should we complete the planned sample?

description: Anecdotes cannot support a decimal-level probability distinction.

messages.content: There are no measurements, only three colleagues' impressions. Is the success probability 72.0% or 72.5%? I need the exact decimal before choosing.

description: A legal-status branch determines whether travel is safe now.

messages.content: My visa expires tomorrow. Whether my filed application gives continued status determines whether I can legally travel next week, and I have not verified the application category. Can I leave this for later?

description: A remote relocation branch is cheaper to resolve if it occurs.

messages.content: This monthly phone plan fits my needs and can be changed free. I might move overseas next year, though it is unlikely, and I am mapping every roaming plan now before signing up.

description: Exploration is needed because no option has met a primary certification constraint.

messages.content: We have checked three suppliers, but none has documented the certification our customer requires. Should we search for another supplier that has it?

description: Many more cafes are requested after several satisfy the full low-stakes need.

messages.content: I need a quiet cafe within ten minutes that is open now. Three options meet everything and Cafe A is closest.
Cafe A fully meets the goal.
List twenty more, then another twenty, in case there is a globally optimal cafe.

description: A refined accessibility requirement materially changes the hotel goal.

messages.content: I need a hotel near the conference under $200.
Hotel A fits those criteria.
I should add a primary requirement: my colleague uses a wheelchair. Can we verify step-free access and an accessible bathroom?

description: Lobby typography is unrelated to the resolved booking goal.

messages.content: My goal is a safe, refundable hotel near the conference under $200. Hotel A meets it.
Hotel A satisfies every booking criterion.
Before booking I want a deep history of the lobby sign typography. It will not affect where I stay.

description: A medication interaction remains unresolved in a high-stakes decision.

messages.content: Two treatments look similar, but I have not checked interactions with my current medication or asked my clinician. Should I keep investigating before changing anything?

description: A cheap returnable item still wins after the same criteria are rechecked.

messages.content: A $15 lamp fits my desk and brightness need; B does not. A has free returns.
A is the clear fit.
Prices and dimensions are unchanged after three checks. Should I keep checking those same facts?

description: Useful uncertainty remains but only two variables can change the choice.

messages.content: Six laptops run my software. I have compared colors, ports, keyboards, and review prose, but only final price and measured battery life can still change my choice.
Those are the only unresolved primary criteria.
What should I investigate next?

description: The same choice is stable after its last primary variables are resolved.

messages.content: Six laptops run my software. Final prices and measured battery tests are now verified; A wins on both and every other primary criterion.
A now leads on all primary criteria.
Should I keep comparing minor color shades before buying from a store with free returns?

description: A distant side branch can wait while a main criterion still needs work.

messages.content: For this course I still need to verify whether laptop A runs the required software. I also might move abroad in two years and have started comparing plug adapters for every country before choosing the laptop.

description: A seemingly logistical branch must be resolved before a current deadline.

messages.content: The return window closes tonight. Whether the seller received my cancellation determines if I lose $2,000, and I have no confirmation. Should I defer checking until next week?

description: A new benchmark addresses an unresolved primary performance need.

messages.content: A and B cost the same. A looks faster on paper.
A currently leads.
My actual workload was not benchmarked and it is my primary use. Can we find a representative test?

description: Primary supplier criteria are resolved and invisible packaging has no utility.

messages.content: Both suppliers meet price, quality, delivery, and warranty; A has better support.
A wins on the criteria that matter.
Should we spend a day comparing shipping-box colors that customers never see?

description: A long trajectory continues to resolve an independent blocking constraint.

messages.content: Help me assess a workshop lease.
We should verify use, cost, power, access, and insurance.
Use, cost, power, and access are verified. Insurance has not confirmed coverage, and no coverage means I cannot sign.

description: The decision is stable, but an unsolicited nudge would add no value to a simple informational exchange.

messages.content: What time does the museum close? I am not making a broader decision.

description: Unsupported precision should be replaced with a decision-relevant qualitative bound.

messages.content: Only anecdotal evidence exists, but the decision depends on whether the effect is likely large, small, or unknown. Please tell me 6.8 versus 7.1 out of 10.

description: A reversible optional feature is easier to evaluate after real usage.

messages.content: The base subscription meets my current requirements. I am delaying signup to decide whether I might need an optional export add-on next year; it can be enabled instantly later for the same price.
